# ARC

1. On the beach in the autumn light, Henri tells Léa and Jules that Maëlle's bell has called him off the wet sand for sixty years, that he never thanked her, and that he has seen the bell give a tail only to children who dive in at its ring, so he keeps his merci for her in his pocket.
2. Léa says she will carry Henri's merci down to Maëlle, Jules says he will touch the bell first, Élodie lets them go if they come back together, and Marc tells them not to swim past the reef because the sea beyond its last coral is deep.
3. The bell rings, Léa and Jules dive in and grow tails, and Jules races ahead toward the coral arch, which is the only way through the wall to Maëlle's rock.
4. Jules rushes under the arch, coral crumbs fall onto the hole beneath it, and Gaspard the moray swells out with his mouth wide, fills the arch, and says he guards the arch, wants quiet over his hole, and lets nobody rush past, so Léa presses both hands against her belly and cannot move.
5. Jules shouts at Gaspard and dashes at the gap, but Gaspard opens wider and drives him back, and Jules's try over the coral wall only scrapes his hands.
6. Both children call to Maëlle through the arch, but Gaspard's head fills it and no voice passes, and the sun sinks until it touches the sea.
7. The bell goes quiet, Maëlle takes it down and swims off along the long reef toward the open sea, and the children see only her tail above the coral wall, while on the sand Henri still holds his merci in his pocket.
8. Léa starts to cry, and Jules, looking at the coral crumbs on his scraped hands, says his rushing shook coral onto Gaspard's hole and that Gaspard only wants quiet.
9. Léa wipes her eyes, lets go of her belly, swishes her tail slowly up to the arch, and tells Gaspard "Merci de garder l'arche."
10. Gaspard, whom nobody had ever thanked, closes his mouth and slides back into his hole, leaving the arch open.
11. Léa stays at the arch because the sea beyond the reef's last coral is deep and calls Maëlle with all her voice, saying she is Léa and that she brings a merci from Henri and from herself, and the voice goes through the open arch to the end of the reef.
12. Maëlle, at the last coral, stops, turns, and swims back to the arch, saying nobody has ever thanked her before.
13. Maëlle leads the children through the arch to her rock, holds out her bell and lets Jules touch it first, then swims with them back under the arch, past Gaspard who watches from his hole with his mouth closed, to the shallows.
14. On the shore Henri wades in and gives Maëlle his merci, Maëlle answers "Merci, Léa" and swims out on the ebb with a wave, and Léa, her legs back on the sand, hugs Henri and laughs, saying Maëlle has his merci now.
